questions.prompt: What stellar property relationship (Leavitt's) does Keating say makes Cepheids useful distance indicators?
choices: A Mass equals luminosity exactly always.
B A period–luminosity relationship: how often they brighten/dim tracks luminosity.
C Color alone with no timing.
questions.explain: Cepheid period-luminosity lets astronomers infer luminosity then distance.

questions.prompt: Who does Keating credit for discovering Cepheids in the Magellanic Clouds and enabling relative distances?
choices: A Only Edwin Hubble working alone.
questions.explain: Leavitt's Magellanic Cloud Cepheid work underpins the period-luminosity law.

questions.prompt: Vera Rubin and Kent Ford's galaxy rotation curves, per Keating, indicate:
choices: A All mass is in visible stars alone.
B Unseen matter (dark matter) is needed to explain high orbital speeds.
C Gravity stops at the galactic edge.
questions.explain: Flat/high rotation curves imply dark matter beyond luminous mass.

questions.prompt: Contrasting MACHOs, what does WIMP stand for in Keating's lecture?
questions.explain: WIMP = weakly interacting massive particle—a dark-matter candidate class.

questions.prompt: Keating ends by joking that we are not mainly "star stuff" but rather:
choices: B Mostly water / Big Bang stuff.
questions.explain: He notes bodies are mostly water and "Big Bang stuff," not mainly iron.
